name: Palette

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Grenache and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Grenache, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.

sheet.soil: Thin, stony limestone scree on the Langesse limestone.

claims.claim: Palette is a small appellation in Provence, a few kilometers east of Aix-en-Provence.
The appellation covers about 50 hectares, strictly delimited.
French Wikipedia gives 52 hectares planted in 2024: 25 red, 19 white, 8 rosé.
The vines grow in Aix-en-Provence, Meyreuil and Le Tholonet. The hamlet of Palette lies in Le Tholonet.
The AOC Palette was classified by decree on 28 April 1948. It extended the earlier recognition of Château Simone, obtained by Jean Rougier in 1946.
Soils are scree (éboulis) from limestone, on the calcaires de Langesse.
Soils are thin, stony and skeletal, on Lutetian Tertiary limestones, including lake limestones.
Vines sit mostly on hillsides facing Mont Sainte-Victoire.
The site is a wooded bowl, sheltered from the wind by nearby heights.
White Palette is at least 80% Clairette. Bourboulenc, Trebbiano, Grenache blanc and Muscat varieties may make up the rest.
Red and rosé Palette is at least 80% Grenache, Mourvèdre and Cinsault.
Yields are capped at 40 hl/ha. Wines must reach at least 11% alcohol.
Harvest is by hand, and winemaking must happen inside the delimited area.
Producers include Château Simone, Château Crémade and Château Henri Bonnaud. Château de Meyreuil and Château des Trois Sautets are also listed.
Château Simone is the best-known Palette estate.
